'''Karl Schlögl''' (October 5, 1924 – May 4, 2007) was an Austrian chemist. He was [[professor]] of [[organic chemistry]] at the [[University of Vienna]] and secretary as well as vice-president of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]].

==Biography==
Schlögl was born October 5, 1924, in [[Vienna]]. Schlögl's first contact with [[organic chemistry]] happened during his middle-school education, when his father - the principal and teacher for natural sciences - took young Karl to school after hours to do experiments together.<ref name="zbp">{{Cite web |title=Ausstellung 1924 - Karl Schlögl |url=http://www.zbp.univie.ac.at/webausstellung/1924/Karl_Schloegl.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303183302/http://www.zbp.univie.ac.at/webausstellung/1924/Karl_Schloegl.htm |archive-date=2016-03-03 |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=www.zbp.univie.ac.at |url-status=dead }}</ref> Schlögl graduated from high-school in 1943 and was declared unfit for service by the [[Wehrmacht]] due to his [[asthma]].
He started studying [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Vienna]] under [[Ernst Späth]], where he completed his [[dissertation]] in 1950.

From 1954 to 1955 Schlögl began working on [[ferrocene]]s at the [[University of Manchester]] during a British council [[scholarship]].
After his return to the [[University of Vienna]] he achieved the [[habilitation]] for [[organic chemistry]] in 1959.

In 1970 Schlögl was promoted to associate professor and in 1971 to full professor for [[organic chemistry]].<ref>Heinz Falk: Karl Schlögl. Obituary. Mh. Chem., 138 (2007)</ref>

Since 1974 he was director, and since 1978 chairman of the [http://www.univie.ac.at/orgchem/ Institute of Organic Chemistry] at the [[University of Vienna]]. From 1977 through 1979 he was the first elected [[dean (education)|Dean]] of the  [[faculty (university)|Faculty]] of Formal and Natural Sciences at the [[University of Vienna]].

The [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] elected Schlögl as a corresponding member in 1978 and as a full member in 1982.<ref>[http://www.oeaw.ac.at/english/about/personen/mitglieder.html Austrian Academy of Sciences, Academy Members] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130627190259/http://www.oeaw.ac.at/english/about/personen/mitglieder.html |date=2013-06-27 }}</ref> From 1991 to 1995 Schlögl was general secretary of the academy, and from 1997 to 2000 he was vice-president of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]]. Furthermore, Schlögl was a corresponding member of the Nordrhein-Westfälische Akademie der Wissenschaften as well as the [[New York Academy of Sciences]].

==Published works==
Schlögl was one of the pioneers of the research into the geometric structure of organic compounds and the resulting mechanisms of their chemical reactions. He has been very successful with his work on new pharmaceutical substances.<ref>Heinz Falk: Karl Schlögl, Nachruf. Almanach d. Öst. Akademie der Wiss., 157, 469-477 (2008)</ref>

Schlögl authored and co-authored over 200 scientific publications and was an inventor on four patents.<ref name="zbp"/> He supervised 51 [[dissertation]]s of his [[doctoral]] students.

Schlögl's main field of research since about 1963 was [[stereochemistry]], and in 1970 he began to shift his focus specifically on the [[Chirality (chemistry)|chirality]] of organic compounds.

==Awards==
Schlögl received numerous scientific awards for his work, including the [[Erwin Schrödinger Prize]] of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] in 1985,<ref name="OeAW - List of awardees of the Erwin Schrödinger Prize">{{cite web|url=http://www-97.oeaw.ac.at/cgi-bin/stipref/web_preise?action=liste&preis=6|language=German|title=Preisträger und Preisträgerinnen des Erwin Schrödinger-Preises|publisher=[[Austrian Academy of Sciences]]|accessdate=24 August 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110819194302/http://www-97.oeaw.ac.at/cgi-bin/stipref/web_preise?action=liste&preis=6|archivedate=19 August 2011}}</ref> the prize for natural sciences of the city of [[Vienna]] in 1989, and the [[Wilhelm Exner Medal]] of the Austrian Economic Association in 1991.<ref>Editor, ÖGV. (2015). Wilhelm Exner Medal. Austrian Trade Association. ÖGV. Austria.</ref>
